description: Ask the classic Magic 8-Ball any yes-or-no question and watch it shake out an answer from a built-in set of twenty playful replies. Pure entertainment that runs entirely in your browser with no sign-up or data collection.

faq.a: Not at all — answers are picked at random from a fixed list. It's a game, not fortune-telling.
No. Your question never leaves your browser and is forgotten the moment you close the tab.
Twenty, mixing positive, negative and mysterious replies — just like the classic toy.
faq.q: How many answers does the ball know?

howTo: Type any yes-or-no question into the box.
Click “Shake the ball” (or press Enter).
Read the ball's verdict and ask again anytime.
name: Magic 8-Ball
tagline: Ask a question — the ball decides

description: Enter two names to reveal a playful compatibility percentage, computed with a deterministic formula so the same pair always gets the same score. A big heart meter and a cheeky verdict make it perfect for sharing with friends.

faq.a: No — it's a playful number-crunching game on the two names. Real compatibility takes actual conversations, not calculators.
The formula is deterministic by design, so a pair's score stays consistent no matter who runs it or how many times.
faq.q: Why do the same names always give the same score?

faq.a: No — the names are sorted before scoring, so order never matters.
faq.q: Does swapping the name order change the score?

howTo: Enter the first name.
Enter the second name.
Click Calculate and share the heart-meter result.
name: Love Calculator
tagline: Playful compatibility score from two names

description: Play the timeless game of Rock Paper Scissors against a computer that picks randomly every round. Wins, losses and draws are tallied live, with a round-by-round history so you can settle any playground debate.

faq.a: It picks one of the three moves at random each round, so no pattern can beat it.
The score lives only for your current session — refreshing the page starts it over.
Rock crushes scissors, scissors cuts paper, paper covers rock. Same move is a draw.

howTo: Click rock, paper or scissors.
See the computer's move and who won the round.
Keep playing — the scoreboard tracks everything.
name: Rock Paper Scissors
tagline: Beat the computer, track your score

description: The computer picks a secret number between 1 and 100 and you hunt it down with hot-and-cold hints after every guess. Your attempt count is tracked and your personal best is kept for the session, so every replay is a chance to beat it.

faq.a: Burning hot means you're within 5, warm within 12, cold within 25, and freezing is further away — plus whether to go higher or lower.
It's kept in memory for your current session only; a fresh page load resets it.
Using binary search (halving the range each time) you can always find it in 7 guesses or fewer.
faq.q: What's a good number of attempts?

howTo: A secret number between 1 and 100 is picked for you.
Enter a guess and read the hot/cold hint.
Keep guessing until you nail it in as few tries as possible.
name: Number Guessing Game

description: Play Tic-Tac-Toe as X against a computer opponent that blocks your threats and grabs winning lines when it spots them. Full score tracking for you, the computer and draws, with instant new rounds.

faq.a: It takes an immediate win when available and blocks your winning lines, otherwise preferring the centre and corners.
Yes — it doesn't play perfectly, so sharp play (especially forks) can still beat it.
No, the scoreboard resets when the page reloads.
faq.q: Is the score saved between visits?

howTo: You play X and always move first — click any square.
The computer answers with O.
First to three in a row wins; start a new round anytime.
name: Tic-Tac-Toe

description: Take a 30-second typing test on a built-in paragraph: the timer starts with your first keystroke and live WPM and accuracy update as you type. Each character is colour-coded so you can see mistakes instantly, with a final scorecard at the end.

faq.a: Standard method: every 5 correct characters count as one word, divided by the minutes typed.
No — it starts with your first typed character, so you can get comfortable first.
faq.q: Does the timer start when I click?

faq.a: Yes, one fixed paragraph, so repeated attempts are directly comparable.
faq.q: Is the paragraph always the same?

howTo: Start typing in the box — the 30-second timer begins automatically.
Watch your live WPM and accuracy update.
When time runs out, review your scorecard and try again.
name: Typing Test

description: Test your reflexes: press start, wait for the pad to turn green, then click as fast as you can. Your reaction time is measured in milliseconds, with your best and average across the last five rounds.

faq.a: The round is voided — you'll need to start that round again. No cheating the green!
faq.q: What happens if I click too early?

faq.a: Most people land between 200 and 300 ms. Under 200 ms is genuinely quick.
It is — the delay is randomised between about 1 and 4 seconds so you can't anticipate it.
faq.q: Why does the wait feel random?

howTo: Press Start — the pad turns red.
Wait without clicking until it turns green.
Click instantly; repeat to build your best-of-5 average.
name: Reaction Time Test
tagline: Wait for green, then click — in ms

description: Flip a virtual coin with a smooth spinning animation and a running tally of heads versus tails. Great for settling decisions, picking teams or just watching the odds even out over many flips.

faq.a: Yes — heads and tails each have a true 50/50 chance on every flip.
Only for your current session; it resets when you leave the page.
The button pauses during the animation so each flip lands cleanly.
faq.q: Can I flip while it's spinning?

howTo: Click “Flip the coin”.
Watch the coin spin and land on heads or tails.
Check the live tally to see how the odds stack up.
name: Coin Flip

description: A simple notepad that auto-saves everything you type to your browser's local storage, so your notes survive a refresh. Live word, character and line counts are shown, and you can download the note as a .txt file anytime.

faq.a: Only in your browser's local storage on this device — nothing is uploaded to any server.
Yes, as long as you don't clear site data. For anything important, use the .txt download as a backup.
faq.q: Will my notes survive a browser restart?

faq.a: No — the notepad is intentionally offline and private, so notes stay on this device.
faq.q: Can I sync notes across devices?

howTo: Type or paste your notes — they save automatically.
Watch the live word, character and line counts.
Download the note as a .txt file or clear it when done.
name: Online Notepad

description: A clean to-do list for capturing tasks: add items in one keystroke, tick them off, delete or filter by active and done. Everything persists in your browser's local storage so your list is still there tomorrow.

faq.a: Completely — they're stored only in your browser's local storage and never sent anywhere.
Yes. They persist on this device until you delete them or clear site data.
faq.q: Do tasks survive closing the browser?

faq.a: Tasks stay in the order you added them; tick off or delete items to keep the list tidy.

howTo: Type a task and press Enter (or Add).
Click the checkbox to mark it done.
Use the All / Active / Done filters and clear completed when finished.
name: To-Do List
tagline: Tasks with filters, saved in your browser

description: Instantly reveals your public IP address — the address websites see when you visit them. If the lookup service is unreachable, you'll get a friendly offline message with a retry button instead of a broken page.

faq.a: No — it's fetched and displayed only. The tool keeps no logs and sends nothing to our servers.
If you use a VPN, proxy or mobile data, the tool shows the address your connection exits through, not your home router's.
faq.q: Why does it show a different address than I expect?

faq.a: You'll see a clear message explaining the service couldn't be reached — check your connection and tap “Try again”.

howTo: Open the tool — your IP is looked up automatically.
Copy it with the Copy button if you need it.
Hit Refresh to re-check anytime.
name: What Is My IP

description: Displays your screen resolution, live viewport size, colour depth, pixel ratio, platform, language and full user agent string — all read locally from your browser. Resize the window and watch the viewport numbers update in real time.

faq.a: No — every value is read from your browser's own APIs and displayed locally.
faq.q: Is any of this sent to a server?

faq.a: Screen is your whole display; the viewport is just the browser window's content area, which shrinks with toolbars and window size.
faq.q: Why do screen and viewport differ?

faq.a: How many physical screen pixels make up one CSS pixel — 2x on most modern phones, 1x on many desktops.

howTo: Open the tool — your device details appear instantly.
Resize the browser window to see the viewport update live.
Copy the user agent string if you need it for debugging.
name: Screen & Device Info
